findings.body:
**Update parent-owned slots after checkout removal.**

A child can reuse a parent-owned slot through `find()`. With no optional removal hook, `removed()` checks only the child's local slots at `src/shared/checkoutWriterContext.ts:197`. The inherited slot remains bound to the deleted checkout.

The parent's `complete()` then fails when it reads the deleted directory. The slot remains incomplete and requires reconciliation. Propagate removal to the parent, as `begin()` and `bindCoordinates()` already do.
findings.title: Update parent-owned slots after checkout removal.

findings.body:
**Restore the metadata that existed before this admission.**

At `src/shared/checkoutWriterContext.ts:267`, compensation restores acquisition-time `entry.metadata`. If `bindCoordinates()` has since bound an initially unbound PR slot, and admission of another slot fails, this write erases that valid binding. The checkout still exists, but its PR slot becomes unbound.

Record the pre-admission metadata in `written` and restore that value. Do not restore the initial `Entry` snapshot.
findings.title: Restore the metadata that existed before this admission.
Re-check the context before installing an acquired slot.

findings.body:
**Do not treat leader closure as process-group termination.**

In `src/shared/proc.ts`, a same-group descendant can ignore SIGTERM and redirect its stdio. If the leader exits, `child.close` resolves even though that descendant survives. Node's close event does not establish that the process group is empty. ([nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html))

Line 679 then skips SIGKILL. During invocation cancellation, Line 531 also removes the group from the exit sweep. The surviving descendant can continue work after cancellation.

Track group termination separately from leader closure. Preserve escalation for a surviving group through the TERM grace period.
findings.title: Do not treat leader closure as process-group termination.

findings.body:
**Keep a still-open child tracked until its close event, or do not release the slots.**

When SIGKILL does not close the child within `killGraceMs`, `terminateGracefully` returns `'killed'` at `src/shared/proc.ts:691`. The child can still be open. A descendant that starts a new session is outside the process-group signal and can keep the inherited stdout pipe open. Node emits `'close'` only after the stdio streams close.

`spawnManaged` registers every child with `trackCheckoutWriter(child)` (`src/shared/proc.ts:510`). `CheckoutWriterContext.track` keeps the child's close promise in `#children` until `'close'` fires (`src/shared/checkoutWriterContext.ts:301-308`). While that set is nonempty, `close()` throws `checkout writer children have not closed` before it sets `retired` or closes any slot (`checkoutWriterContext.ts:311-314`).

Callers that call `close()` without checking `pendingChildren` then fail with the slots still held: `src/adapters/git/slotWorktreeRegistry.ts:109` and `src/ops/review/internal/addressCheckoutOwnership.ts:301, 312, 365, 493`. The caller at `src/adapters/git/prWorktree.ts:863` checks `pendingChildren` and skips `close()`, so its slots also stay held.

The fix belongs in the finalization callers, not in the kill ladder. Return an outcome that tells callers the child is still open. Then either wait for the tracked close before releasing slots, or leave the slots held with an explicit owner. Policy for this state belongs to the plan runner.

<details>
<summary>Scope of this finding</summary>

The finding covers only children that remain open after the SIGKILL rung. A child that closes within the grace window is not affected. Whether the specific unguarded finalizers run while such a child is still open was not traced. The call from `src/driver/claude-code/cli.ts:238` was also not traced to its checkout context.

</details>
findings.title: Keep a still-open child tracked until its close event, or do not release the slots.
